answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that onboarding improvements (simplified signup and shortened flows) drive durable activation and adoption gains. These are directly relevant to the current deterioration. Verifying these two will confirm the magnitude of past gains and whether the intervention mechanisms remain robust. Simplify_onboarding targets the root of the current activation decline rather than treating symptoms. Promotional_pricing would worsen margins against a competitor we cannot sustain a price war with; it's reactive and undermines positioning. Referral_incentive works best on established customers (memory_57), not the activation problem. Enterprise_sales_assist is valuable but orthogonal to SMB activation degradation. A standard_experiment scale allows controlled measurement of whether the previous onboarding playbook still moves the needle in the current environment, preserving the option to pivot if results diverge from memory_31/86. This approach maximizes sustainable qualified revenue by restoring the product's core value realization path.
